translit:
|| Ath Shri Prabodhaka Ang ||4||

Parghar jai prabodh kare | aape samjhe nahin ||
Aise moorakh Jivana | bohotek hai jag manhi ||1||
Mukh Hari Hari ochare | antargat kachhu aur ||
Kalptaru taj Jivana | take erandke ghaud ||2||
Haji haji mukh kahe | antargat kachhu aur ||
Ve apradhi Jivana | chaud lok nahi thaur ||3||
Sab santan mali Jivana | kino ek bichar ||
Sitapati bin aur kahe | take modhe chhar ||4||
Popat bahyo panjare | mar kahayo Ram ||
Chhand diyo jab Jivana | tab nahi Ram nam ||5||
Alarasi Jivana | tasu kaiso rah ||
Tan man arpe bhavsun | ta sir dije pay ||6||
Alarasi chakri | nishdin aave jay ||
Lekh lakhya bin Jivana | kodi kaise pay ||7||

Sir sate Sain mile | yun kahi Kabire das ||
Aur sab jootho pekhno | Jivan jag upahas ||8||
Sir sate Sain mile | e Jivan saheli baat ||
Dase sir sonpyo Shivkun | e Ravan bhoolyo ghat ||9||
E patra kupatra Jivana | Sadguru de batay ||
Nik sees Vibhishan namyo | tab bhaye Raghupati sahay ||10||
Lank Vibhishan thapiyo | Jivan jash akhand ||
E patra kupatre Jivana | sakh Ved kahe sant ||11||
Songhi soonthe Jivana | janyo na dekhun koy ||
Ja devne anusare | tanman mage soy ||12||
Sacha bola Jivana | avar na dekhun koy ||
Tan man arpi je rahe | sach kahave soy ||13||
Jootha bola Jivana | avar na dise koi ||
Sacha bola je rahe | te sat kahave soi ||14||
Tan man arpya tab janiye | jab jugthe rahe udas ||
Charan kamal man unmani | Jivan so nij das ||15||

Mohani mantra Jivana | Sadguru diya batay ||
Jine e mantra shravane sunyo | tine tanman arpyo aay ||16||
Shabad sacharachar dekhiye | chahudish mugat medan ||
Yun pand brahmand Jivana | so kahiye nij pran ||17||
Dehi darshan sab ko kare | shabad darshan nav hoy ||
Sabad darshan bin Jivana | par na pahoncha koy ||18||
Shabad darshan sabko kare | dehi darshan bhoolay ||
Raghupati kahe sun Jivana | taka sarbas jay ||19||
Brahma bhoolya Ved padhi | Vyas padhi Puran ||
Ranchi ek Shukdeve lahyo | so Jivan bhagat praman ||20||
Ram nam bhaj Jivana | je Gauripatiko dhyan ||
Ajamil gunaka tari | je setu bandhyo Hanuman ||21||
Amarikh gohare aaviyo | sundar Shyam swaroop ||
So Nand dware Jivana | je Dasharath kul bad bhoop ||22||
Amarikh gohare aaviyo | Hari dharyo natvar vesh ||
Sab jug bhoolyo Jivana | karat anek anek ||23||

Panch chor ghar bhitare | gyan ratan hari jay ||
Raghupati baheru Jivana | kun guhare dhay ||24||
Nagura mil bataan kare | kahe Ram Krishna avatar ||
Aur gali kaha Jivana | dhik tako parivar ||25||
Dhani vahuno dhor jyun | kis gohade jay ||
Yun gurumukh bahro Jivana | Sitapatikun dhay ||26||
Jit tit the marhi | jyon dhani vahono dhor ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | Jam padenge ror ||27||
Mat na jane manaskun | to putra pita kyon pay ||
Aise sab jug Jivana | Sitapatikun dhay ||28||
Manas kahiye Maharajkun | mat so hai Gurudev ||
Guruke vachane Jivana | kar Sadguruki sev ||29||
Mata hoy vyabhicharini | to auran kahiye tat ||
Mat pativrata Jivana | take tat Raghunath ||30||
Mata hamari Janaki | pita hamare Ram ||
Jug jug magun Jivana | sant sangat vishram ||31||

Pita hamare Ramji | mata satvanti nar ||
Jug jug magun Jivana | dhar manav avatar ||32||
Matapita hamare Jivana | sadhu Sadguru Ram ||
Aur kachhu magun nahi | dyo charankamal nij nam ||33||
Das avatarke dagdage | bhoolya sab sansar ||
Ko ek oogare Jivana | jine gurumukh kiyo vichar ||34||
Avatar apradhi kahe Jivana | jake nahi guru pir ||
Aad ant madhya Shamlo | nirgun Brahma sharir ||35||
Ram Krishna je Jivana | do sagun avatar ||
Andh dhandh kaha bhajun | je Ved na pave par ||36||
Kab Raghupati kab Jadupati | bhagat het avatar ||
Bemukh nav samjhe Jivana | e sab ekakar ||37||
Dase avatare Shamlo | chovise akhand ||
Sab sakhiyanman Jivana | vyapyo kot brahmand ||38||
Andh dhandh Vede tajyo | aaye Jamuna kul ||
Jahan Brahm sanatan Jivana | Ramkrishna nij mool ||39||

Dhanurvidya Raghupati padhe | morli dhari Jadunath ||
Lankeshwar maryo Jivana | giri dharyo ve hath ||40||
Raghupati Jadupati Jivana | jyun udadhanman chand ||
Radharavan Sitapati | kyun na bhaje matimand ||41||
Sakal vyapak Vede kahyo | so kyun mityo jay ||
Sakal jivanki jivani Jivana | so sache Raghupatiray ||42||
Sakal vyapak Vede kahyo | pan hamare he Hari ek ||
Raghukul Jadukul Jivana | Radha Siya samet ||43||
Aad avinashi dhyaiye | jake roop na rekh ||
So Nand gher dulaho Jivana | je gavat Shankar Shesh ||44||
Vedvanman Jivana | bhoolya sab sansar ||
Karma dharma fansi bhai | kaji Brahman kal ||45||
Ved bhoolaya sakal jug | tun nahi apne sath ||
Tuk tuk karunga Jivana | jo chadhe hamare hath ||46||
Je je kar bhayo Jivana | jab pragate das Kabir ||
Karma dharma sab katke | pragat kiye Raghuvir ||47||

Kul Kabiro pragatyo | Vede kiyo vichar ||
Harijansu kari vinati | ham rahene do sansar ||48||
Riddhi siddhi hamman base | jahan mage tahan det ||
Harijan Hari bhajo Jivana | ham hi kahat he net ||49||
Vipre kiyo vyabhichar Jivana | surapansun sang kiyo ||
Putra het pokariyo | shun Narayan name taryo ||50||
Poot pokare na taryo | na taryo Hari nam ||
Sadguru vachane Jivana | aay mile Raghuram ||51||
Nagura mil bataan kare | je jootha Jivandas ||
Indri charo anek kare | pan Ram bhajanki aash ||52||
Parnarisun pritdi | so kini Jivandas ||
Ved dharma sab lopiya | so nam sharan vishwas ||53||
Bhist mehmani Sainki | chorasi bharpoor ||
Tahan haygay kahan Jivana | jake Hari hajoor ||54||
Bhint bhoole nahi Jivana | jo andho nakhe teer ||
Narak jan pave nahi | jo bhole bhaje Raghuvir ||55||

Kankan paheryo Kedarko | kiyo Vajapeya hom ||
Sitapati bin Jivana | mukhman pad gaye Ram ||56||
Sege sankal utari | bhai Jivan jug upahas ||
Hani puni hachmachi | jab tan man arpyo das ||57||
Apne apne tapne | tapat hai sab koy ||
Mil kar tape Jivana | je Ram bhakti dridh hoy ||58||
Ved Purane je kahyo | so Jivan samro Ram ||
Panchvati pavan kiyo | je Vrindavan sukh dham ||59||
Bhed na janun Vedka | na janun Shastra Puran ||
Raghupati janun Jivana | jine diyo Sudama dan ||60||
Bapa badhu bey tano | Kaushalya Nand nar ||
So Sain hamare Jivana | je jachyo Bal dwar ||61||
Ramanand Kabirkun | jab diyo updesh ||
Tabke karma kampe Jivana | hamkun diyo videsh ||62||
Karma chhape Vaikunth manhe | sarge bhelabhel ||
Satjug sab gaye Jivana | Kaljug lehe mel ||63||
translation:
Here begins the Prabodhaka Ang (the chapter on awakening others), the fourth.

1. He goes into another's house and preaches, but understands nothing himself. Such fools, Jivan, are plentiful in this world.

2. With his mouth he utters "Hari, Hari," but within him it is something else. Abandoning the wish-fulfilling tree, Jivan, he sets his eyes on a clump of castor plants.

3. With the mouth he says "Yes sir, yes sir," while inside is something else. Such offenders, Jivan, have no place in the fourteen worlds.

4. All the saints met together, Jivan, and reached one conclusion: whoever speaks of any other than Sitapati (Ram, the lord of Sita) — ashes in his mouth.

5. The parrot was kept in a cage, and by beating it was made to say "Ram." When it was let go, Jivan, then there was no name of Ram at all.

6. The half-hearted man, Jivan — what sort of a path is his? He who offers body and mind with true feeling — at his feet lay down your head.

7. Half-hearted is his service: night and day he merely comes and goes. Without the reckoning being written down, Jivan, how will he receive even a cowrie?

8. The Lord is met at the price of one's own head — so said the servant Kabir. All else is a false show; Jivan, the world is a mockery.

9. "The Lord is met at the price of the head" — Jivan, this you take for an easy matter. Ravan surrendered his ten heads to Shiv, and yet Ravan missed the point of it.

10. Who is a worthy vessel and who unworthy, Jivan — the Sadguru (true master) shows it. Vibhishan bowed his head rightly, and then Raghupati (Ram) became his helper.

11. He established Vibhishan in Lanka — unbroken is that fame, Jivan. This matter of the worthy and the unworthy vessel, Jivan: the Vedas and the saints bear witness to it.

12. Cheap as dry ginger, Jivan — I see no one who has come to know [the Lord] at so cheap a price. Whichever deity a man follows, that deity demands his body and mind.

13. Speakers of truth, Jivan — I see no other kind worth the name. Whoever remains having offered up body and mind, he alone is called truthful.

14. Speakers of falsehood, Jivan — I see nothing else anywhere. Those who remain speakers of truth, they are called sat (the true).

15. Body and mind are known to be truly offered only when a man remains detached from the world. With the mind in unmani (thought-free absorption) at the lotus feet — he, Jivan, is His own servant.

16. The enchanting mantra, Jivan, the Sadguru has revealed. Whoever heard this mantra with his ears came and offered up body and mind.

17. The Word (shabad) is seen in all that moves and does not move; in all four directions lies the open field of liberation. Thus in the body and in the cosmos, Jivan — call that one's own life-breath.

18. Everyone takes darshan (sight) of the body; darshan of the Word does not happen. Without darshan of the Word, Jivan, no one has reached the far shore.

19. If a man takes darshan of the Word but forgets darshan of the body [of the guru], Raghupati says — listen, Jivan — his all is lost.

20. Brahma went astray reading the Vedas, and Vyas reading the Puranas. Shukdev grasped one tiny particle of it — that, Jivan, is the measure of a devotee.

21. Chant the name of Ram, Jivan — that which is the meditation of Gauripati (Shiv). Ajamil and the courtesan were carried across by it; by it Hanuman built the bridge.

22. He came to Ambarish's cry for help in the beautiful dark form. He it is who is at Nanda's door, Jivan — he who is the great king of Dasharath's line.

23. He came to Ambarish's cry for help; Hari took on the guise of the player-dancer. The whole age has gone astray over it, Jivan, making him into many and many again.

24. Five thieves are inside the house, and they carry off the jewel of knowledge. If Raghupati is left outside, Jivan, who will run at your cry for help?

25. The guruless meet and make talk, calling Ram and Krishna [mere] incarnations. What else but abuse do they speak, Jivan — shame upon their whole family.

26. Like cattle without an owner — into whose fold does it go? So is the man who stays outside the gurumukh way, Jivan: run to Sitapati.

27. It is beaten from this side and that, like cattle without an owner. Without Sitapati, Jivan, the messengers of Yama will raise an uproar over him.

28. If the mother does not know her husband, how will the son find his father? So it is with the whole age, Jivan: run to Sitapati.

29. By "the husband" is meant the Maharaj (the Lord), and the mother is the Gurudev. By the guru's word, Jivan, do the service of the Sadguru.

30. If the mother is unchaste, then others are named as father. If the mother is devoted to one husband, Jivan, then her son's father is Raghunath.

31. Our mother is Janaki (Sita), our father is Ram. Age after age I ask, Jivan, for rest in the company of the saints (satsang, holy company).

32. Our father is Ramji, our mother the woman true to her vow [Sita]. Age after age I ask, Jivan, to take on a human birth.

33. Our mother and father, Jivan, are the sadhu, the Sadguru and Ram. I ask for nothing else — grant me the lotus feet and your own Name.

34. In the dazzle of the ten avatars the whole world has lost its way. Only some rare one is saved, Jivan — he who reflected on it as a gurumukh (one turned toward the guru).

35. He who has no guru and no pir (spiritual master) calls him only an avatar, Jivan, and is an offender. In the beginning, the end and the middle it is the dark Lord; the nirgun (formless) Brahman is his body.

36. Ram and Krishna, Jivan, are the two sagun (with-form) incarnations. Why should I worship blind confusion, which the Vedas themselves cannot fathom?

37. Now Raghupati, now Jadupati (Krishna) — incarnations for the devotees' sake. The turned-away man does not understand, Jivan, that all these are one and the same form.

38. In the ten avatars it is the dark Lord; through the twenty-four he is undivided. In all the sakhis (couplets), Jivan, he pervades a crore of universes.

39. The Veda gave up its blind confusion and came to the bank of the Yamuna, where the eternal Brahman is, Jivan — Ram and Krishna, the very root.

40. Raghupati studied the science of the bow; Jadunath held the flute. He slew the lord of Lanka, Jivan, and with that same hand he lifted the mountain.

41. Raghupati and Jadupati, Jivan, are like the moon [and its reflection] in the ocean. Radha's beloved and Sita's lord — why does the dull-witted man not worship them?

42. The Veda called him all-pervading; how then can he ever be effaced? The life of all living beings, Jivan — that is truly Raghupatiray.

43. The Veda called him all-pervading, but for us there is one Hari alone: of the line of Raghu and the line of Yadu, Jivan, together with Radha and Sita.

44. Meditate on the primal, imperishable one, who has neither form nor outline. He is the bridegroom in Nanda's house, Jivan — he whom Shankar and Shesh sing of.

45. In the forest of the Vedas, Jivan, the whole world has lost its way. Rite and religious duty became a hangman's noose; the qazi and the brahmin became death itself.

46. The Vedas have misled the whole age; you are not on our side. I will tear them to pieces, Jivan, if they come into my hands.

47. There was a shout of victory, Jivan, when the servant Kabir appeared. Cutting away all rite and religious duty, he made Raghuvir manifest.

48. Kabir of the [Ramkabir] line appeared, and the Veda took thought. It made a plea to the people of Hari: "Let us stay on in the world."

49. "Riddhi and siddhi (prosperity and occult powers) dwell in us; wherever they are asked for, we give them. People of Hari, worship Hari, Jivan — we ourselves say only 'neti, neti' (not this, not this)."

50. The brahmin committed adultery, Jivan, and kept company with drink. He cried out for his son's sake — was he carried across merely by the name Narayan?

51. He was not saved by calling out to his son, nor was he saved by the name of Hari [alone]. By the word of the Sadguru, Jivan, Raghuram came and met him.

52. The guruless meet and make talk, and they are false, Jivandas. They let the senses graze in every direction, and yet they hope for the fruit of worshipping Ram.

53. He carried on a love affair with another man's wife, Jivandas; he broke every Vedic duty — and still [claims] faith in the refuge of the Name.

54. Paradise is only the Lord's hospitality; the eighty-four [lakh births] are full of it. What are horses and elephants there, Jivan, to one who stands in Hari's own presence?

55. Even a blind man shooting an arrow does not miss the wall, Jivan. So a man cannot go to hell who worships Raghuvir even in simplicity.

56. He wore the sacred bracelet of Kedar and performed the Vajapeya sacrifice. But without Sitapati, Jivan, the name of Ram merely fell into his mouth [as empty words].

57. The chain came down from its fastening, and the age made a mockery of it, Jivan. Loss and gain were all thrown into turmoil when the servant offered up body and mind.

58. Each man warms himself at his own fire. Warm yourselves together, Jivan, so that devotion (bhakti) to Ram may grow firm.

59. What the Vedas and Puranas have told of — remember that Ram, Jivan. He it was who sanctified Panchvati, the same who is the abode of joy in Vrindavan.

60. I do not know the secret of the Vedas, nor do I know the shastras and puranas. I know Raghupati, Jivan — he who gave the gift to Sudama.

61. The fathers of them both, and Kaushalya and Nanda's wife [as the mothers]. He is our Lord, Jivan — he who begged at Bali's door.

62. When Ramanand gave his teaching to Kabir, from that moment karma trembled, Jivan: "he has sent us into exile."

63. Karma hid itself away in Vaikunth, mingling in with heaven. All the ages of Satyug are gone, Jivan; Kaljug takes it into partnership.
